title: U.S. Senate · Oregon

context.text: Incumbent Jeff Merkley defeated Paul Damian Wells 93.2%-6.2% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. David Brock Smith, a sitting Oregon state senator, won a seven-candidate Republican primary with 29.5% of the vote, ahead of Jo Rae Perkins (27.1%) and Brent Barker (23.3%). Gary Dye is the Libertarian Party nominee and Chris Henry is the Pacific Green Party and Progressive Party nominee.

summary.text: Jeff Merkley is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election. A Stanford and Princeton graduate who worked on defense policy and then in affordable housing, he served in the Oregon House (1999-2009, Speaker 2007-2009) before winning his Senate seat in 2008. He was re-elected in 2014 and 2020 and says he is focused on health care, housing, education and jobs.

background.text: Born in Myrtle Creek, Oregon, where his father worked as a millwright; the family later moved to Roseburg and then East Multnomah County. He graduated from David Douglas High School.

Became the first in his family to graduate from college, earning a bachelor's degree in international relations from Stanford University in 1979 and a Master of Public Affairs from Princeton University's Woodrow Wilson School in 1982.

Interned for Sen. Mark Hatfield, then worked on nuclear disarmament and military spending issues in Washington, D.C., including as a Presidential Management Fellow at the Office of the Secretary of Defense and as an analyst at the Congressional Budget Office.
Returned to Portland and served as executive director of Portland Habitat for Humanity (to 1994), then developed affordable housing for the nonprofit Human Solutions.
Elected to the Oregon House of Representatives in 1998 and served from 1999 to 2009. He was elected House Democratic leader after the 2003 session and Speaker in 2007.
Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2008, defeating incumbent Gordon Smith, and re-elected in 2014 and 2020. According to his Senate office, he holds the seat once held by Mark Hatfield.

Sits on the Appropriations, Environment and Public Works, Budget, Rules and Foreign Relations committees, chairing the Appropriations subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies and an Environment and Public Works subcommittee; he is also co-chair of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China.
According to his Senate office, he holds a town hall in each of Oregon's 36 counties every year, and he lives in East Portland with his wife, Mary Sorteberg; they have two children.

priorities.text: Describes his role as fighting to restore the American Dream and standing up for middle-class families, focused on equal opportunity for children and a fair shot for people who work hard, 'no matter where they started in life.'
Lists agriculture, health care, jobs and the economy, natural resources and rural development, consumer and taxpayer protection, and tackling climate change among his issue priorities.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Chemical Safety, Waste Management, Environmental Justice, and Regulatory Oversight), the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on Appropriations (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies), the Committee on Rules and Administration, and is Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on the Budget.

summary.text: David Brock Smith is the Republican nominee and a sitting Oregon state senator from Port Orford. A small-business owner who took over his family's restaurant, he held local office, served on the Curry County Board of Commissioners, and was elected to the Oregon House in 2016 before moving to the state Senate in 2023. His campaign says he is running to bring a rural voice to Washington.

background.text: Born in Port Orford, Oregon, in 1976 or 1977. He is a third-generation Southwest Oregon resident, according to his campaign website.
Earned an associate degree from Southwestern Oregon Community College and a bachelor's degree from Southern Oregon University.
Worked in the culinary industry in the Rogue Valley, then took over his family's Port Orford restaurant, the Port & Starboard, from his parents, according to his campaign website.
Served on the Port Orford City Council (including as president), the school board, the Curry County Planning Commission, and as president of the North Curry County Chamber of Commerce.
Elected to the Curry County Board of Commissioners in 2012.
Elected to the Oregon House of Representatives in 2016 (District 1) and served from January 2017 to January 2023.

Appointed to the Oregon State Senate for District 1 in January 2023, succeeding Dallas Heard, and elected to a full term in 2024. In the 2021-2022 session he was vice chair of the House Energy and Environment Committee.
Won the Republican primary for U.S. Senate on May 19, 2026.

record.text: As an Oregon state legislator, served on the House and Senate Natural Resources and Wildlife Recovery, Agriculture and Natural Resources, and Energy and Environment committees across multiple sessions (2017-2024), including as vice chair of the House Energy and Environment Committee (2021-2022).

candidates.name: Gary Dye

summary.text: Gary Dye is the Libertarian Party nominee. A Portland native and engineer, he has worked in oil refining and natural gas measurement and says he has sat on the board of the Libertarian Party of Oregon. He has run for office several times, including as the Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate in 2020.

background.text: Born in Portland, Oregon, and attended David Douglas schools, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
Earned degrees from Oregon State University (chemical engineering, 1981), Pepperdine University (MBA, 1989) and the University of California, Irvine (bachelor's degree, 1991).

Worked as a process engineer in oil refineries, including four years in Saudi Arabia, then as a gas measurement engineer and director for a utility in the natural gas industry; his Ballotpedia profile lists his profession as engineering consultant.
Has served on the board of directors of the Libertarian Party of Oregon and on the David Douglas School District's Citizens Budget Committee, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
Ran as the Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate in 2020, finishing behind Jeff Merkley and Jo Rae Perkins, and in the nonpartisan 2022 primary for Metro Council President.

candidates.researchNotes: Dye has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no 2026 campaign website or statements were found; background is drawn from Ballotpedia biography and an earlier (2024) survey response not reused here for positions.

candidates.name: Chris Henry

summary.text: Chris Henry (also known as Kit) is the Pacific Green Party and Progressive Party nominee. A community advocate whose career includes work as a union truck driver and aircraft mechanic, he ran for Multnomah County Commission in 2024. Little other biographical detail is public.

background.text: Says in his Ballotpedia survey that he was the ninth of twelve children and that his grandfather, Kevin McCann, was President Eisenhower's speechwriter.
Graduated from the UAW Trade School in 1985; career experience includes work as a union truck driver, aircraft mechanic and community advocate.
Has been affiliated with Honest Elections Oregon.
Ran in the May 21, 2024, nonpartisan primary for Multnomah County Commission District 1, which Meghan Moyer and Vadim Mozyrsky advanced from.

candidates.researchNotes: Henry has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no current U.S. Senate campaign website or statements were found; his 2024 survey answers on file addressed a different (local Portland) candidacy and are not reused here.
